```text
**Title:** "Move the "Add webhook", "Link account" and admin notice "Operations" menus to <aria-menu>"
**State:** Open
**Labels:** enhancement, scope: medium
**Assignee:** Jack-Donohue
**Author:** Jack-Donohue (collaborator)
**Milestone:** Sprint 2
**Comments:** 2

**Body summary:** The issue asks to make three settings menus keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible by converting them from Fomantic UI dropdowns to `<aria-menu>` elements:

- **Webhook "Add webhook" menu:** Changed in the shared webhook list template, covering repository, organization, user, and admin pages. Its items come from the link menu template.
- **New webhook form type switcher:** Converted to `<aria-menu>` and given a accessible name combining a localized "webhook type" label with the current type. This needs a new locale key.
- **"Link account" menu on the security settings page:** Converted to `<aria-menu>`, with each OAuth2 provider linking to its sign-in URL.
- **Admin system notices "Operations" menu:** Converted to `<aria-menu>`, opening upward, with select-all, deselect-all, and invert-selection actions.

The acceptance criteria require standard keyboard behavior (open, arrow navigation, type-ahead, Escape to close), no visual change in light or dark themes (with before/after screenshots), and Playwright and Go integration tests passing. Two open questions remain: whether the new locale key name is acceptable, and whether the 11-item webhook type menu needs a maximum height with scrolling. The design decisions favor changing the two shared templates rather than each settings page, and naming the switcher through an `aria-label` rather than adding visible text.
```

```text
Move the "Add webhook", "Link account" and admin notice "Operations" menus to <aria-menu>
---
### User Story

As a keyboard or screen reader user configuring a repository, organisation, account or the site, I want the menus that add a webhook, link an external account or act on admin notices to be operable from the keyboard, so that settings pages don't block me in the places I configure integrations.

### User Scenario

An organisation owner using a screen reader opens **Settings → Webhooks**. They Tab to **Add webhook**, press Enter, type "s" twice to move from "Slack" to the next item starting with "s", and press Enter to open the new webhook form. On that form the type switcher at the top is read as "Webhook type: Slack, menu button", and they use it to switch to "Discord". Later they open **Settings → Security**, open **Link account** and choose a sign-in provider. A site admin opens **Site administration → System notices**, opens **Operations** above the table and picks "Select all".

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given the webhook list on the repository, organisation, user and admin settings pages (all rendered by `templates/repo/settings/webhook/base_list.tmpl`), when it renders, then **Add webhook** is an `<aria-menu>` whose items are the links from `templates/repo/settings/webhook/link_menu.tmpl`, and it has no `ui dropdown` class.
- [ ] AC2: Given the new webhook form (`templates/webhook/new.tmpl`), when it renders, then the type switcher is an `<aria-menu>`. Its trigger is named with both a localised "webhook type" label and the current type, not the type name alone.
- [ ] AC3: Given at least one OAuth2 sign-in source, when **Settings → Security** renders, then the **Link account** menu (`templates/user/settings/security/accountlinks.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>` and each provider item navigates to its `/user/oauth2/<name>` URL.
- [ ] AC4: Given **Site administration → System notices**, when it renders, then the **Operations** menu (`templates/admin/notice.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>` that opens upwards (`placement="top-start"`). "Select all", "Deselect all" and "Inverse selection" change the table checkboxes by keyboard and by mouse.
- [ ] AC5: Given each migrated menu, when operated by keyboard, then Enter/Space/ArrowDown opens it with focus on the first item, the arrows, Home/End and first-letter type-ahead move focus, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
- [ ] AC6: Given light and dark themes, when the migrated menus are compared before and after, then their position and look are the same, including the webhook icons. The PR includes before/after screenshots.
- [ ] AC7: Playwright tests cover adding a webhook from the repository settings page and switching the webhook type, both by keyboard. The existing e2e and Go integration suites still pass.

### Out of Scope

- Webhook form fields themselves (the content type and HTTP method `<select>`s and the events checkboxes).
- The admin list filter menus ("Sort", "Filter") in `templates/admin/*/list.tmpl`: they show a current selection, so they stay Fomantic like the other filters.
- Adding new webhook types or providers.

### Open Questions

- The AC2 label needs a new locale key, as no existing key says "webhook type". Is `repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher` an acceptable name? (A new key goes into `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` only.)
- `link_menu.tmpl` lists 11 webhook types. Is type-ahead enough, or should the menu also get a maximum height and scroll?

### Design Decision

### Decision 1: where to make the change
**Decision:** Change the two templates that wrap `link_menu.tmpl` (`base_list.tmpl` and `webhook/new.tmpl`), not each settings page. That one change covers the repository, organisation, user and admin webhook pages.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Change each settings page's template separately.
- (b) Leave the webhook menus on Fomantic and add only the missing names through the existing ARIA patch.

**Rationale:** All four pages already include `base_list.tmpl`, so (a) would copy the same markup four times and risk the copies drifting apart. (b) leaves the VoiceOver arrow key problem in `aria.md` unfixed. Upstream is also removing Fomantic (go-gitea/gitea#29849).

**Consequences:** Easier: one template change, one e2e test on the repository page, and the other three pages are covered by sharing the markup. Harder: `link_menu.tmpl` must keep its outer `.menu` element to be a valid `<aria-menu>` child, so it can't be reused as a plain list anywhere else without that wrapper.

### Decision 2: naming the type switcher
**Decision:** Give the new webhook form's type switcher an `aria-label` that combines a "webhook type" label with the current type.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Let the trigger take its name from its visible text, the current type alone.
- (b) Add a visible "Type:" text label next to the switcher.

**Rationale:** `aria.md` says a menu that only shows its current value needs a name of its own. "Slack, menu button" doesn't tell the user that the button switches the type. (b) also fixes that, but it changes the page's look, which AC6 rules out for this issue.

**Consequences:** Easier: the trigger is clear to screen readers and nothing changes visually. Harder: the label can fall out of sync with the visible text if someone later changes one and not the other, so the template should build both from the same `HookType` value.

### Scope

medium

*Spec drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) from the remaining `ui dropdown` menus on `main` (90fe0b7f42), posted by @Jack-Donohue.*
```

```text
     1	import {generateElemId, hideElem, showElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
     2
     3	// A menu button following https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/ with no Fomantic.
     4	// Markup: <aria-menu><button type="button">label</button><div class="menu"><a class="item">...</a></div></aria-menu>
     5	// Optional host attributes, read only by CSS: placement="bottom-start|bottom-end|top-start|top-end" (default bottom-start), pointing
     6	// Items get real focus (roving tabindex) instead of aria-activedescendant, see web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md
     7	window.customElements.define('aria-menu', class extends HTMLElement {
     8	  trigger!: HTMLElement;
     9	  popup!: HTMLElement;
    10	  inited = false;
    11
    12	  connectedCallback() {
    13	    // in <head>-loaded components, the children are not parsed yet while the page is still loading
    14	    if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    15	      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init, {once: true});
    16	    } else {
    17	      this.init();
    18	    }
    19	  }
    20
    21	  disconnectedCallback() {
    22	    document.removeEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init);
    23	    if (this.inited) this.close(false); // also removes the outside click listener
    24	  }
    25
    26	  init = () => {
    27	    if (this.inited) return;
    28	    const popup = this.querySelector<HTMLElement>(':scope > .menu');
    29	    const trigger = Array.from(this.children).find((el) => el !== popup) as HTMLElement | undefined;
    30	    if (!popup || !trigger) return;
    31	    this.inited = true;
    32	    this.popup = popup;
    33	    this.trigger = trigger;
    34
    35	    if (trigger.tagName !== 'BUTTON') {
    36	      trigger.setAttribute('role', 'button');
    37	      trigger.tabIndex = 0;
    38	    }
    39	    if (!popup.id) popup.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-popup-');
    40	    trigger.setAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'menu');
    41	    trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    42	    trigger.setAttribute('aria-controls', popup.id);
    43	    popup.setAttribute('role', 'menu');
    44	    if (!popup.hasAttribute('aria-label') && !popup.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby')) {
    45	      if (!trigger.id) trigger.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-trigger-');
    46	      popup.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', trigger.id); // keeps the menu's name once focus is on an item
    47	    }
    48	    hideElem(popup);
    49	    this.updateItemRoles();
    50
    51	    trigger.addEventListener('click', () => this.isOpen() ? this.close(true) : this.open('first'));
    52	    trigger.addEventListener('keydown', this.onTriggerKeyDown);
    53	    trigger.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    54	    popup.addEventListener('keydown', this.onPopupKeyDown);
    55	    popup.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    56	    popup.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    57	      // bubble phase, so the item's own click handlers have already run
    58	      if ((e.target as Element).closest('[role="menuitem"]')) this.close(true);
    59	    });
    60	  };
    61
    62	  // items may be added after init, e.g. by a feature script, so refresh them on every open
    63	  updateItemRoles() {
    64	    for (const child of this.popup.children) {
    65	      if (child.classList.contains('item')) {
    66	        child.setAttribute('role', 'menuitem');
    67	        child.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
    68	      } else if (child.classList.contains('divider')) {
    69	        child.setAttribute('role', 'separator');
    70	      } else {
    71	        child.setAttribute('role', 'none');
    72	      }
    73	    }
    74	  }
    75
    76	  items(): HTMLElement[] {
    77	    // hidden items can't take focus, so leaving them in would stall opening and arrow keys
    78	    return Array.from(this.popup.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(':scope > [role="menuitem"]:not(.tw-hidden)'));
    79	  }
    80
    81	  isOpen() {
    82	    return this.trigger.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
    83	  }
    84
    85	  open(focus: 'first' | 'last') {
    86	    this.updateItemRoles();
    87	    showElem(this.popup);
    88	    this.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    89	    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDownOutside, {capture: true});
    90	    const items = this.items();
    91	    (focus === 'first' ? items[0] : items.at(-1))?.focus();
    92	  }
    93
    94	  close(restoreFocus: boolean) {
    95	    // only restore when focus is still in the popup, so focus moved elsewhere by an item handler is kept
    96	    const focusInPopup = this.popup.contains(document.activeElement);
    97	    hideElem(this.popup);
    98	    this.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    99	    document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDownOutside, {capture: true});
   100	    if (restoreFocus && focusInPopup) this.trigger.focus();
   101	  }
   102
   103	  onPointerDownOutside = (e: Event) => {
   104	    if (!this.contains(e.target as Node)) this.close(false);
```

```text
  const onAuthNameChange = function () {
    // appSubUrl is either empty or is a path that starts with `/` and doesn't have a trailing slash.
    document.querySelector('#oauth2-callback-url')!.textContent = `${window.location.origin}${appSubUrl}/user/oauth2/${pathEscape(elAuthName.value)}/callback`;
  };
  elAuthName.addEventListener('input', onAuthNameChange);
  onAuthNameChange();
}

function initAdminNotice() {
  const pageContent = document.querySelector('.page-content.admin.notice');
  if (!pageContent) return;

  const detailModal = document.querySelector<HTMLDivElement>('#detail-modal')!;

  // Attach view detail modals
  queryElems(pageContent, '.view-detail', (el) => el.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const elNoticeDesc = el.closest('tr')!.querySelector('.notice-description')!;
    const elModalDesc = detailModal.querySelector('.content pre')!;
    elModalDesc.textContent = elNoticeDesc.textContent;
    showFomanticModal(detailModal);
  }));

  // Select actions
  const checkboxes = document.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('.select.table .ui.checkbox input');

  queryElems(pageContent, '.select.action', (el) => el.addEventListener('click', () => {
    switch (el.getAttribute('data-action')) {
      case 'select-all':
        for (const checkbox of checkboxes) {
          checkbox.checked = true;
        }
        break;
      case 'deselect-all':
        for (const checkbox of checkboxes) {
          checkbox.checked = false;
        }
        break;
      case 'inverse':
        for (const checkbox of checkboxes) {
          checkbox.checked = !checkbox.checked;
        }
        break;
    }
  }));

  document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#delete-selection')?.addEventListener('click', async function (e) {
    e.preventDefault();
    this.classList.add('is-loading', 'disabled');
    const data = new FormData();
    for (const checkbox of checkboxes) {
      if (checkbox.checked) {
        data.append('ids[]', checkbox.closest('.ui.checkbox')!.getAttribute('data-id')!);
      }
    }
    await POST(this.getAttribute('data-link')!, {data});
    window.location.reload();
  });
}
```

````text
func TestNewWebHookLink(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	require.NoError(t, db_model.Insert(t.Context(), &webhook.Webhook{
		RepoID:      1,
		URL:         "http://localhost/gitea-test-webhook-link",
		ContentType: webhook.ContentTypeJSON,
		Events:      `{}`,
		IsActive:    true,
	}))
	hook := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &webhook.Webhook{RepoID: 1})
	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
	webhooksBaseHref := "/user2/repo1/settings/hooks"
	cases := []string{
		webhooksBaseHref,
		webhooksBaseHref + "/gitea/new",
		webhooksBaseHref + "/" + strconv.FormatInt(hook.ID, 10), // edit webhook
	}
	for _, reqHref := range cases {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", reqHref), http.StatusOK)
		htmlDoc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		menus := htmlDoc.doc.Find(".ui.top.attached.header .ui.dropdown .menu a")
		menus.Each(func(i int, menu *goquery.Selection) {
			foundHref := menu.AttrOr("href", "")
			assert.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(foundHref, webhooksBaseHref))
		})
	}
}

// testAPICreateWebhookForRepo returns the created hook, whose ID is the only safe way to
// find it again: the url column is TEXT, which MSSQL refuses to compare in a WHERE clause.
func testAPICreateWebhookForRepo(t *testing.T, session *TestSession, userName, repoName, url, event string, branchFilter ...string) *api.Hook {
	token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, session, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeAll)
	var branchFilterString string
	if len(branchFilter) > 0 {
		branchFilterString = branchFilter[0]
	}
	req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/"+userName+"/"+repoName+"/hooks", api.CreateHookOption{
		Type: "gitea",
		Config: api.CreateHookOptionConfig{
			"content_type": "json",
			"url":          url,
		},
		Events:       []string{event},
		Active:       true,
		BranchFilter: branchFilterString,
	}).AddTokenAuth(token)
	resp := MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)
	return DecodeJSON(t, resp, &api.Hook{})
}

func testCreateWebhookForRepo(t *testing.T, session *TestSession, webhookType, userName, repoName, url, eventKind string) {

so we add IDs to all the Fomantic UI checkboxes automatically by JS. If the `label` part is empty,
then the checkbox needs to get the `aria-label` attribute manually.

# The `<aria-menu>` Web Component

New action menus (a button that opens a list of choices, with no search input and no selection state)
should use `<aria-menu>` from `web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts` instead of a Fomantic dropdown.
It follows the ARIA menu button pattern and moves real focus onto the items (roving `tabindex`),
so the VoiceOver arrow key problem above cannot happen. Try it on the `/devtest/aria-menu` page.

```html
<aria-menu>
  <button type="button">Actions</button> <!-- first non-.menu child is the trigger -->
  <div class="menu">
    <a class="item" href="...">...</a>
    <div class="divider"></div>
    <div class="item">...</div> <!-- Enter, Space and click all fire the item's "click" -->
  </div>
</aria-menu>
```

The popup opens below the trigger, aligned to its start. Two optional host attributes, read only by CSS, move it:

* `placement="bottom-start|bottom-end|top-start|top-end"`, the same words as `data-tooltip-placement`.
  The template knows where the menu sits, so there is no automatic flip: a menu at the right edge needs `bottom-end`.
* `pointing` draws Fomantic's small arrow on a bottom placement.

Put `data-tooltip-content` on the trigger, not the host, so the tooltip text also becomes the trigger's `aria-label`.
The tooltip will not show while the menu is open.

Comboboxes, searchable and multiple-selection dropdowns still use Fomantic Dropdown below.
````

```text
/** Generate a random alphanumeric string. */
export function randomString(length: number): string {
  const chars = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789';
  let result = '';
  for (let index = 0; index < length; index++) {
    result += chars.charAt(Math.floor(Math.random() * chars.length));

function apiAuthHeader(username: string, password: string) {
  return {Authorization: `Basic ${globalThis.btoa(`${username}:${password}`)}`};
}

export function apiHeaders() {
  return apiAuthHeader(env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD);
}

async function apiRetry(fn: () => Promise<{ok: () => boolean; status: () => number; text: () => Promise<string>}>, label: string) {
  const maxAttempts = 5;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    const response = await fn();
    if (response.ok()) return;
    if ([500, 502, 503].includes(response.status()) && attempt < maxAttempts - 1) {
      const jitter = Math.random() * 500;
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000 * (attempt + 1) + jitter));
      continue;
    }
    throw new Error(`${label} failed: ${response.status()} ${await response.text()}`);
  }
}
```

```text
---
scope: options/locale, modules/translation, crowdin.yml
verified-at: b32c95c2b0
---

# i18n — locale files and translation

**Read when:** adding or changing any user-visible string.
**Not here:** using a key in a template -> `templates.md`; in TypeScript -> `frontend-js.md`.

## Responsibilities

The translated strings and the machinery that looks them up, for both the backend/templates and
the frontend.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` | **the only file you edit** — the source of truth |
| `options/locale/locale_<lang>.json` | 28 other locales, all generated from Crowdin |
| `modules/translation/translation.go` | locale loading and lookup; requires the `locale_*.json` naming |
| `modules/translation/i18n/` | the lookup implementation and fallback behaviour |
| `crowdin.yml` | the sync config: source is `locale_en-US.json`, translations land as `locale_%locale%.json` |

## Conventions & invariants

- **Only ever edit `locale_en-US.json`.** Every other locale file is written by Crowdin
  (`crowdin.yml` sets `en-US` as the source). Editing one by hand is overwritten on the next sync,
  and a PR that touches other locale files will be asked to revert them.
- Keys are dotted and grouped by area (`repo.issues.new`, `settings.`, `admin.`). Put a new key
  next to its neighbours rather than at the end.
- Templates use `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "key"}}`, or `TrN` for plurals. TypeScript uses `trN` from
  `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts`; strings reach the frontend through `window.config.i18n`
  (`templates/base/head_script.tmpl`), which is deliberately limited to general text — anything
  specialised should arrive via an API response, a `data-` attribute, or `pageData`.
- A plural is **two keys** suffixed `_1` and `_n`, both interpolating `%d` — see
  `actions.runs.graph_jobs_count_1` and `_n`. `TrN` and `trN` pick the form from the count.
- A `data-` attribute carrying a translated string to TypeScript is read with `getAttribute` and
  usually named for its use (`data-tooltip-content`, read in `web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts`). Vue
  mounts often use `data-locale-<name>`, as `templates/repo/actions/view_component.tmpl` does for
  both plural forms.
- **Never write a user-visible literal** in a template, a handler, or a `.ts` file.
- Errors whose message reaches the user go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`
  (`modules-util-and-generics.md`), not a plain `fmt.Errorf`.
- `crowdin.yml` sets `skip_untranslated_strings` and `export_only_approved`, so a missing
  translation falls back rather than shipping an empty string.

## Recipes

**Add a string.** Add the key to `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` in the right group, use it via
`ctx.Locale.Tr` or `trN`, and leave the other locale files alone.

**Add a plural.** Two keys named `<key>_1` and `<key>_n` plus `TrN` / `trN`; the count argument
selects the form.

**Add a string the frontend needs.** Prefer a `data-` attribute or `pageData` from the handler.
Only genuinely general text belongs in the global `window.config.i18n` object.

## Gotchas

- A missing key renders as the key itself — visible in the UI but easy to miss on a rarely-hit
  branch.
- Changing an existing key's *text* is fine; changing the *key name* invalidates every existing
  translation for it.
- Only a `bindata` build embeds `options/locale` (`modules/options/options_bindata.go`) and needs a
  rebuild for a locale change. A plain build reads the files from disk at startup
  (`modules/options/options_dynamic.go`), and outside `RUN_MODE = prod` reloads them on change
  (`modules/translation/translation.go` → `WatchLocalChanges`).
- Some keys are built from an enum's name while rendering: `actions.status.%s`
```

```text
// DisplayName returns the friendly name for this provider
func (b *BaseProvider) DisplayName() string {
	return b.displayName
}

// IconHTML returns icon HTML for this provider
func (b *BaseProvider) IconHTML(size int) template.HTML {
	svgName := "gitea-" + b.name
	switch b.name {
	case "gplus":
		svgName = "gitea-google"
	case "github":
		svgName = "octicon-mark-github"
	}
	svgHTML := svg.RenderHTML(svgName, size)
	if svgHTML == "" {
		log.Error("No SVG icon for oauth2 provider %q", b.name)
		svgHTML = svg.RenderHTML("gitea-openid", size)
	}
	return svgHTML
	return p.sourceName
}

func (p *AuthSourceProvider) IconHTML(size int) template.HTML {
	if p.iconURL != "" {
		img := fmt.Sprintf(`<img class="tw-object-contain" width="%d" height="%d" src="%s" alt="%s">`,
			size,
			size,
			html.EscapeString(p.iconURL), html.EscapeString(p.DisplayName()),
		)
		return template.HTML(img)
	}
	return p.GothProvider.IconHTML(size)
}

// Providers contains the map of registered OAuth2 providers in Gitea (based on goth)
// key is used to map the OAuth2Provider with the goth provider type (also in AuthSource.OAuth2Config.Provider)
// value is used to store display data
var gothProviders = map[string]GothProvider{}

func addOAuth2Source(t *testing.T, authName string, cfg oauth2.Source) {
	cfg.Provider = util.IfZero(cfg.Provider, "gitea")
	err := auth_model.CreateSource(t.Context(), &auth_model.Source{
		Type:     auth_model.OAuth2,
		Name:     authName,

}
```

```text
  // do not init "custom" dropdowns, "custom" dropdowns are managed by their own code.
  registerGlobalSelectorFunc('.ui.dropdown:not(.custom)', (el) => {
    const $dropdown = fomanticQuery(el);
    if ($dropdown.data('module-dropdown')) return; // do not re-init if other code has already initialized it.

    $dropdown.dropdown('setting', {hideDividers: 'empty'});

    if (el.classList.contains('jump')) {
      // The "jump" means this dropdown is mainly used for "menu" purpose,
      // clicking an item will jump to somewhere else or trigger an action/function.
      // When a dropdown is used for non-refresh actions with tippy,
      // it must have this "jump" class to hide the tippy when dropdown is closed.
      $dropdown.dropdown('setting', {
        action: 'hide',
        onShow() {
          // hide associated tooltip while dropdown is open
          this._tippy?.hide();
          this._tippy?.disable();
        },
        onHide() {
          this._tippy?.enable();
          // eslint-disable-next-line unicorn/no-this-assignment
          const elDropdown = this;

          // hide all tippy elements of items after a while. eg: use Enter to click "Copy Link" in the Issue Context Menu
          setTimeout(() => {
            const $dropdown = fomanticQuery(elDropdown);
            if ($dropdown.dropdown('is hidden')) {
              queryElems(elDropdown, '.menu > .item', (el) => el._tippy?.hide());
            }
          }, 2000);
        },
      });
    }
```

````text
## Current sprint: Sprint 2

- **Dates:** Oct 13 – Oct 29, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 29, 11:59 PM**, except
  the D7 check-in, due **Oct 22, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100.
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D8) or no release (D9) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** anything the Sprint 2 page doesn't change comes from the Sprint 1 page, and
  every Sprint 0 standard still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 2` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate before coding | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue, with **at least two alternatives** | 5 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs, each with a `## Tech Debt` section | 20 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 5 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint2/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | UML class and sequence diagrams plus Q&A for one medium issue you resolved | 15 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/diagrams/` |
| D7 | Mid-sprint check-in | 5 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/checkin/<github-username>.md` |
| D8 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint2/report.md` |
| D9 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D10 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Either load can be met with equivalent story points instead. Every
  issue has exactly **one** assignee. Unfinished Sprint 1 issues
  go into the backlog before new work. To skip one, write the reason on that issue (closed, made
  invalid by later changes, or no longer relevant). If the backlog is too thin to meet the load,
  find areas that still need work (features, improvements, test gaps, bugs) and write new issues
  for them the usual way: user story, acceptance criteria and an estimate.
- **D3:** each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and why one won; this is graded
  strictly. The site also accepts the decision in an issue comment or the PR description; the team
  keeps it in the issue body. Decisions that span issues go in `docs/sprint2/design.md`.
- **D4:** every PR description has the Tech Debt section (see "Pull request format"). A PR without
  it loses points. Per-PR scores are combined across your issues and scaled to 20.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. Logs hold the full prompts and output: summaries,
  screenshots and share links are not logs. The link must open the log file itself, not a folder or
  another issue. The folder must exist even if no AI was used; in that case, post a comment saying
  so. The site accepts the link in an issue or a PR comment this sprint; the team keeps it in
  **issue comments only** (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D6:** see "UML diagrams (D6)" below.
- **D7:** about 150 words on each of: what you have done and what remains; one thing you learned
  about the codebase or about software engineering; one thing you would do differently. On time and
  substantive scores 5, late or thin 3, missing 0.
- **D8:** graded on completeness, specificity and quality of evidence; sections are in "Sprint
  report (D8) sections" below.
- **D9:** keep the base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s1` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), tag after every
  Sprint 2 PR is merged, push the tag to origin, and write release notes listing the features,
  fixes and improvements. The site's example says `v2.17.2`; this fork's base is `v1.27.3`.
- **Reviews:** nobody approves or merges their own PR. Reviewers leave substantive comments, not a
  bare approval. Tell the reviewer on Zulip or by email, and aim to review within 24 hours. Each
  student reviews at least one PR per sprint, and every teammate at least once per semester.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR submitted to upstream Gitea that is accepted or under
  active review, at the instructor's discretion.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
```

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
  issue before implementation starts.

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality including the Tech Debt section 4, CI or manual verification 3,
review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric
````

**Issue #110 Open Question 1: which locale key should name the webhook type switcher (AC2)?**

Options:
- **type_switcher with %s (Recommended)** - `repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher`: "Webhook type: %s". One key, and the template passes in the same translated type name it shows on screen, so the label and the visible text can't drift apart. A screen reader reads "Webhook type: Slack, menu button".
- **Plain label key** - `repo.settings.webhook.type`: "Webhook type". The template puts the label and the type name together itself. The key is easier to reuse, but the order and punctuation are fixed in the template and can't be changed per language.

**Issue #110 Open Question 2: should the 11-item webhook menu get a maximum height and scroll?**

Options:
- **No, type-ahead only (Recommended)** - Match the current Fomantic menu, which has no max height. That keeps AC6 (no visual change), and the 11 items (about 400px) fit on screen.
- **Add max-height + scroll** - Cap the height and let the menu scroll. Useful on short screens, but it changes how the menu looks (against AC6) and needs focus-scroll handling.


**Answer:** type_switcher with %s (Recommended), No, type-ahead only (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

```markdown
# Plan: #110 — move "Add webhook", "Link account" and admin notice "Operations" menus to `<aria-menu>`

## Context

Issue #110 (Sprint 2, medium, assigned to Jack-Donohue, spec reviewed by @controlled-opposition) asks for four Fomantic `ui dropdown` action menus on settings pages to become `<aria-menu>`. Fomantic dropdowns keep focus on the wrapper and use `aria-activedescendant`, which breaks VoiceOver arrow keys (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`). `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`) moves real focus between items. #108 (this branch, **not merged yet**) did the same for the Code tab menus, so this plan reuses its pattern.

Decided:
- Open questions: new key `repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher` = `"Webhook type: %s"`. No max height on the 11-item menu.
- Reviewer notes: type-ahead uses "d" twice (Discord → DingTalk) rather than "s" twice. The right-aligned menus get `placement="bottom-end"`. Decision 2 should say why the switcher still counts as an action menu (its items are links).
- Deadline: everything merged by **Oct 29, 11:59 PM** (tomorrow), and the PR needs a teammate review first.

## 0. Setup (before any edits)

- Remind the user to run the session under `specstory run claude`.
- Start the branch from `main`, per COURSE-WORKFLOW ("never merge another feature branch into yours"). #110 doesn't need #108's CSS:
  `git switch main && git pull origin main && git switch -c feat/issue-110-aria-menu-settings`
- Take the **before** screenshots now, on unmodified `main` (AC6): repo hooks list, the new-webhook form, Settings → Security with an OAuth2 source, and Admin → System notices. Each one in light and dark, with its menu open. Use a throwaway Playwright script in the scratchpad at 1280×720, switching themes with `emulateMedia({colorScheme})`. A local DB may have no notices or OAuth2 sources: add one source in Site Admin → Authentication, and insert a few `notice` rows with sqlite.

## 1. Templates (`placement` matches where each menu sits today)

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `templates/repo/settings/webhook/base_list.tmpl` | Keep the `<div class="ui right">` wrapper. Replace `.ui.jump.dropdown` with `<aria-menu placement="bottom-end">`, whose trigger is `<button type="button" class="ui primary tiny button">`, followed by the unchanged `{{template "repo/settings/webhook/link_menu" .}}` (it already outputs `<div class="menu"><a class="item">…`). |
| `templates/webhook/new.tmpl` | Compute `{{$typeName := ctx.Locale.Tr (print "repo.settings.web_hook_name_" ctx.RootData.HookType)}}` once. Replace the `ui right type dropdown` div with `<aria-menu class="ui right" placement="bottom-end">`. Keeping `ui right` on the host preserves the old box: absolute, full header height, so the menu still drops from the header's bottom edge. The trigger is `<button type="button" class="btn" aria-label="{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher" $typeName}}">` containing the icon, `{{$typeName}}` and the caret svg (`dropdown icon`), then `link_menu`. The visible text and the label both come from `$typeName` (Decision 2 consequence). |
| `templates/user/settings/security/accountlinks.tmpl` | Same shape as base_list: `.ui.right` › `<aria-menu placement="bottom-end">` › `<button type="button" class="ui primary tiny button">`, and the existing `.menu` with its `/user/oauth2/{{$key \| PathEscape}}` items unchanged. |
| `templates/admin/notice.tmpl` | `<aria-menu placement="top-start" floating>` › `<button type="button" class="ui small button">Operations</button>` and the existing `.menu` with the three `.item.select.action[data-action]` items unchanged. `initAdminNotice` in `web_src/js/features/admin/common.ts` binds click handlers to `.select.action`, and aria-menu turns Enter/Space into `click()`, so **no JS change**. |

`options/locale/locale_en-US.json`: add `"repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher": "Webhook type: %s"` next to the other `repo.settings.webhook.*` keys. Only this locale file changes.

## 2. CSS for visual parity (AC6): `web_src/css/modules/aria-menu.css`

Each rule copies what Fomantic gives these menus today. To keep merges with #108 small, add them away from #108's caret block (which sits right after `aria-menu > .btn`).
- **Item weight**: add `font-weight: var(--font-weight-normal)` to `aria-menu > .menu > .item`. The Fomantic `.ui.dropdown .menu > .item` sets it. Without it, items inside `h4.ui.header` inherit the medium weight.
- **Item images**: add `aria-menu > .menu > .item > img`, copied from Fomantic's `.ui.dropdown .menu > .item > img` (`dropdown.css` ~L812–841): inline-block, `vertical-align: top`, margin `-0.25rem 0.78571429rem -0.25rem 0`, `max-height: 2em`. Most webhook icons and custom OAuth2 icons are `<img>`, and AC6 names the icons explicitly.
- **`floating` host attribute** (keeps Fomantic's `ui floating` look for the Operations menu): full `border-radius`, plus a 0.5em gap (`margin-top` for bottom placements, `margin-bottom` for top placements). Put it after the placement rules so the full radius wins over the top-only radius. Three more `ui floating dropdown jump` action menus could reuse it later (pulse, dashboard navbar).
- **`.btn` trigger in a header** (type switcher): keep the header's font size and weight, which the old `.text` inherited. The `aria-menu` host resets size to 1rem, and a `<button>` resets weight. Also keep the caret's gap from Fomantic's `.ui.dropdown > .dropdown.icon` (1em at 0.857em size). Tune the exact values against the before screenshots.

Document `floating` in the host-attribute comment at the top of `aria-menu.ts` and in the `<aria-menu>` section of `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`. If any `.claude-students/docs/*.md` lists aria-menu attributes, update it and its `guide/` twin.

## 3. Tests

**Go integration**
- `tests/integration/repo_webhook_test.go` `TestNewWebHookLink`: the selector `.ui.top.attached.header .ui.dropdown .menu a` **will break**. It currently passes even when it finds nothing. Change it to `.ui.top.attached.header aria-menu > .menu > a`, add `assert.NotZero(t, menus.Length())`, and assert `.ui.top.attached.header .ui.dropdown` is absent. This covers AC1/AC2 on the list, new and edit pages.
- `tests/integration/user_settings_test.go` `TestUserSettingsSecurity`: new subtest for AC3. Call `addOAuth2Source(t, "<name>", oauth2.Source{})` (helper in `oauth_test.go`), then assert `aria-menu > .menu > a[href='/user/oauth2/<name>']`.
- New `tests/integration/admin_notice_test.go` (2026 copyright header) for AC4. As user1, request `/-/admin/notices` (the fixtures include 3 notices). Assert `tfoot aria-menu[placement='top-start'] > .menu > .item.select.action` has count 3 and `tfoot .ui.dropdown` is absent.

**Playwright** (AC5/AC7): new `tests/e2e/webhook-menus.test.ts`, following `tests/e2e/repo-menus.test.ts`. Use `apiCreateRepo`, `login`, `randomString` and `assertNoJsError` from `tests/e2e/utils.ts`.
1. *Add webhook by keyboard*, on `/<owner>/<repo>/settings/hooks`:
   - Focus `button "Add Webhook"`, press Enter: the `Gitea` item has focus. End goes to `Packagist`. Escape closes the menu and focus is back on the trigger.
   - Press ArrowDown, then `d`, `d`: focus moves to `Discord`, then `DingTalk`.
   - Check the menu's right edge matches the trigger's (bottom-end).
   - Press Enter: the URL ends in `/dingtalk/new`. Fill the payload URL and submit by keyboard. The list shows the new webhook.
2. *Switch type by keyboard*, on `/settings/hooks/dingtalk/new`:
   - The trigger is named `Webhook type: DingTalk` and its menu has the same name.
   - Press Enter, then `s`: focus moves to `Slack`. Press Enter: the URL ends in `/slack/new` and the trigger is now named `Webhook type: Slack`.

AC4's keyboard and mouse checkbox behaviour has no cheap e2e path: system notices only come from mirror or user-deletion failures. Cover it with the integration test above plus a manual check, and say so in the PR.

## 4. Verification

- `make fmt`, `make lint-go`, `make lint-js`, `make lint-css`, `make lint-templates`, `make lint-json`
- `make frontend` (CSS rebuild), then `pnpm exec vitest web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.test.ts`
- `make test-sqlite#TestNewWebHookLink`, `#TestUserSettingsSecurity`, and the new admin notice test
- `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='tests/e2e/webhook-menus.test.ts' make test-e2e`, and also `menus`, `aria-menu` and `repo-menus` (the existing e2e suite still passes)
- Manual checks in the running app (`run` skill):
  - Repo, org, user and admin webhook pages: the admin page renders `base_list` twice.
  - An edit-webhook page (it renders the switcher).
  - Security page with an OAuth2 source.
  - Notices: Select all, Deselect all and Inverse selection, by mouse and by keyboard. Focus returns to Operations after each.
  - Take the **after** screenshots to pair with the before set.
- `./.claude-students/check.sh` before pushing.

## 5. Things to note in the PR and issue (we have no `gh`, so the user posts these)

- **Issue edits for the user** (Design Decision changes go in the issue body):
  - Scenario: "d" twice.
  - Decision 2: the switcher shows a current value, but its items are links that navigate, so it is an action menu, unlike Sort/Filter.
  - Open Questions answered as above.
- **Tech Debt.** Introduced: the `floating` attribute; fixed placements with no auto-flip. Encountered:
  - Fomantic's default `direction: 'auto'` ignores the `upward` class whenever there's room below, so on short notice lists the old Operations menu opened *downward*. AC4's `top-start` follows the template's intent. Fomantic's leftward flip likewise depended on viewport width. Explain both next to the screenshots.
  - `TestNewWebHookLink` used to pass with zero matches.
- Commits: Conventional Commits ending `(#110)`, with `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5` and no Co-Authored-By or Signed-off-by (AGENTS.md). Each commit only after explicit human approval. Suggested split: `feat(settings): …` for templates, CSS, locale and docs; `test(settings): …` for the tests.
- Draft the PR body in the COURSE-WORKFLOW format, with an AI-assistance section and no log link. Draft the AI Assistance issue comment for the user to post. Remind the user to run `specstory sync` and file the log under `ai-logs/sprint2/Jack-Donohue/`.
```

```text
## Gotchas

- A page-load init without its early return costs every page in Gitea; the 500ms warning catches it.
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
- Which menu to build on, Fomantic dropdown or `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`),
  is decided in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`.
- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
  in `modules/` or `features/`.
- A feature can follow a comment box it did not create: the editor's change and upload events
  bubble (`features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`, `features/comp/EditorUpload.ts`), and
  `getComboMarkdownEditor` finds the editor, as `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` does. But
  the editor attaches itself before its async `init` finishes, and calling it before then throws;
  read its textarea until an event arrives.
- Enter on a Fomantic dropdown item only fires a `click` when the item is a link or carries
  `js-aria-clickable` (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`), so a plain click listener on other
  items never hears a keyboard pick. The close reason menu in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`
  marks its items; an `<aria-menu>` item needs no class, as Enter and Space call its `click()`.
- After a click on a Fomantic dropdown item, the dropdown keeps the focus, so focusing something
  else from your click handler needs `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
```

```text
## Approved Plan:
# Plan: #110 — move "Add webhook", "Link account" and admin notice "Operations" menus to `<aria-menu>`

## Context

Issue #110 (Sprint 2, medium, assigned to Jack-Donohue, spec reviewed by @controlled-opposition) asks for four Fomantic `ui dropdown` action menus on settings pages to become `<aria-menu>`. Fomantic dropdowns keep focus on the wrapper and use `aria-activedescendant`, which breaks VoiceOver arrow keys (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`). `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`) moves real focus between items. #108 did the same for the Code tab menus and has **since been merged** (PR #127), so this plan reuses its pattern and its CSS (the `.ui.button` caret rules in `aria-menu.css`) is already on `main`.

Decided:
- Open questions: new key `repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher` = `"Webhook type: %s"`. No max height on the 11-item menu.
- Reviewer notes: type-ahead uses "d" twice (Discord → DingTalk) rather than "s" twice. The right-aligned menus get `placement="bottom-end"`. Decision 2 should say why the switcher still counts as an action menu (its items are links).
- Deadline: everything merged by **Oct 29, 11:59 PM** (tomorrow), and the PR needs a teammate review first.

Each one in light and dark, with its menu open. Use a throwaway Playwright script in the scratchpad at 1280×720, switching themes with `emulateMedia({colorScheme})`. A local DB may have no notices or OAuth2 sources: add one source in Site Admin → Authentication, and insert a few `notice` rows with sqlite.

## 1. Templates (`placement` matches where each menu sits today)

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `templates/repo/settings/webhook/base_list.tmpl` | Keep the `<div class="ui right">` wrapper. Replace `.ui.jump.dropdown` with `<aria-menu placement="bottom-end">`, whose trigger is `<button type="button" class="ui primary tiny button">`, followed by the unchanged `{{template "repo/settings/webhook/link_menu" .}}` (it already outputs `<div class="menu"><a class="item">…`). |
| `templates/webhook/new.tmpl` | Compute `{{$typeName := ctx.Locale.Tr (print "repo.settings.web_hook_name_" ctx.RootData.HookType)}}` once. Replace the `ui right type dropdown` div with `<aria-menu class="ui right" placement="bottom-end">`. Keeping `ui right` on the host preserves the old box: absolute, full header height, so the menu still drops from the header's bottom edge. The trigger is `<button type="button" class="btn" aria-label="{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher" $typeName}}">` containing the icon, `{{$typeName}}` and the caret svg (`dropdown icon`), then `link_menu`. The visible text and the label both come from `$typeName` (Decision 2 consequence). |
| `templates/user/settings/security/accountlinks.tmpl` | Same shape as base_list: `.ui.right` › `<aria-menu placement="bottom-end">` › `<button type="button" class="ui primary tiny button">`, and the existing `.menu` with its `/user/oauth2/{{$key \| PathEscape}}` items unchanged. |
| `templates/admin/notice.tmpl` | `<aria-menu placement="top-start" floating>` › `<button type="button" class="ui small button">Operations</button>` and the existing `.menu` with the three `.item.select.action[data-action]` items unchanged. `initAdminNotice` in `web_src/js/features/admin/common.ts` binds click handlers to `.select.action`, and aria-menu turns Enter/Space into `click()`, so **no JS change**. |

`options/locale/locale_en-US.json`: add `"repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher": "Webhook type: %s"` next to the other `repo.settings.webhook.*` keys. Only this locale file changes.

## 2. CSS for visual parity (AC6): `web_src/css/modules/aria-menu.css`

Each rule copies what Fomantic gives these menus today. Put each one next to the rules it extends (item rules, placement rules, trigger rules).
- **Item weight**: add `font-weight: var(--font-weight-normal)` to `aria-menu > .menu > .item`. The Fomantic `.ui.dropdown .menu > .item` sets it. Without it, items inside `h4.ui.header` inherit the medium weight.
- **Item images**: add `aria-menu > .menu > .item > img`, copied from Fomantic's `.ui.dropdown .menu > .item > img` (`dropdown.css` ~L812–841): inline-block, `vertical-align: top`, margin `-0.25rem 0.78571429rem -0.25rem 0`, `max-height: 2em`. Most webhook icons and custom OAuth2 icons are `<img>`, and AC6 names the icons explicitly.
- **`floating` host attribute** (keeps Fomantic's `ui floating` look for the Operations menu): full `border-radius`, plus a 0.5em gap (`margin-top` for bottom placements, `margin-bottom` for top placements). Put it after the placement rules so the full radius wins over the top-only radius. Three more `ui floating dropdown jump` action menus could reuse it later (pulse, dashboard navbar).
- **`.btn` trigger in a header** (type switcher): keep the header's font size and weight, which the old `.text` inherited. The `aria-menu` host resets size to 1rem, and a `<button>` resets weight. Also keep the caret's gap from Fomantic's `.ui.dropdown > .dropdown.icon` (1em at 0.857em size). Tune the exact values against the before screenshots.
```

```mjs
// Throwaway AC6 screenshot script for #110, not committed. Usage: node shots.mjs <outdir>
import {createRequire} from 'node:module';
import {mkdirSync} from 'node:fs';

const require = createRequire('/workspaces/gitea/package.json');
const {chromium} = require('@playwright/test');

const outDir = process.argv[2];
mkdirSync(outDir, {recursive: true});
const base = 'http://localhost:3010';
const user = 'shot-admin';
const repo = 'hooks-demo';

const pages = [
  {name: 'hooks-list', url: `/${user}/${repo}/settings/hooks`, open: (p) => p.getByText('Add Webhook', {exact: true}).first()},
  {name: 'hook-new', url: `/${user}/${repo}/settings/hooks/gitea/new`, open: (p) => p.locator('h4.ui.top.attached.header').getByText('Gitea', {exact: true}).first()},
  {name: 'security', url: `/user/settings/security`, open: (p) => p.getByText('Link Account', {exact: true}).first()},
  {name: 'notices', url: `/-/admin/notices`, open: (p) => p.getByText('Operations', {exact: true}).first()},
];

const browser = await chromium.launch();
for (const colorScheme of ['light', 'dark']) {
  const context = await browser.newContext({viewport: {width: 1280, height: 720}, colorScheme});
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto(`${base}/user/login`);
  await page.fill('#user_name', user);
  await page.fill('#password', 'password123!');
  await page.click('form button.primary');
  await page.waitForURL((u) => !u.pathname.startsWith('/user/login'));
  for (const {name, url, open} of pages) {
    await page.goto(`${base}${url}`);
    const trigger = open(page);
    await trigger.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    await page.screenshot({path: `${outDir}/${name}-${colorScheme}-closed.png`});
    await trigger.click();
    await page.waitForTimeout(400); // Fomantic animates the menu in
    await page.mouse.move(0, 0); // no hover highlight on an item
    await page.screenshot({path: `${outDir}/${name}-${colorScheme}-open.png`});
  }
  await context.close();
}
await browser.close();
```

```mjs
// Throwaway AC6 geometry dump for #110, not committed. Usage: node metrics.mjs > out.json
import {createRequire} from 'node:module';

const require = createRequire('/workspaces/gitea/package.json');
const {chromium} = require('@playwright/test');

const base = 'http://localhost:3010';
const user = 'shot-admin';
const repo = 'hooks-demo';

const pages = [
  {name: 'hooks-list', url: `/${user}/${repo}/settings/hooks`, open: (p) => p.getByText('Add Webhook', {exact: true}).first()},
  {name: 'hook-new', url: `/${user}/${repo}/settings/hooks/gitea/new`, open: (p) => p.locator('h4.ui.top.attached.header').getByText('Gitea', {exact: true}).first()},
  {name: 'security', url: `/user/settings/security`, open: (p) => p.getByText('Link Account', {exact: true}).first()},
  {name: 'notices', url: `/-/admin/notices`, open: (p) => p.getByText('Operations', {exact: true}).first()},
];

const round = (r) => r && Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(r).map(([k, v]) => [k, Math.round(v * 10) / 10]));

const browser = await chromium.launch();
const page = await (await browser.newContext({viewport: {width: 1280, height: 720}})).newPage();
await page.goto(`${base}/user/login`);
await page.fill('#user_name', user);
await page.fill('#password', 'password123!');
await page.click('form button.primary');
await page.waitForURL((u) => !u.pathname.startsWith('/user/login'));
const out = {};
for (const {name, url, open} of pages) {
  await page.goto(`${base}${url}`);
  const trigger = open(page);
  await trigger.evaluate((el) => el.scrollIntoView({block: 'center'}));
  // the visible trigger box: Fomantic's dropdown element, or the <aria-menu> button
  const triggerEl = await trigger.evaluateHandle((el) => el.closest('aria-menu > :not(.menu)') ?? el.closest('.ui.dropdown') ?? el);
  const triggerBefore = round(await triggerEl.evaluate((el) => el.getBoundingClientRect().toJSON()));
  const triggerStyle = await triggerEl.evaluate((el) => {
    const s = getComputedStyle(el);
    const caret = el.querySelector('.dropdown.icon');
    const text = [...el.querySelectorAll('*')].find((c) => c.children.length === 0 && c.textContent.trim()) ?? el;
    const ts = getComputedStyle(text);
    return {fontSize: ts.fontSize, fontWeight: ts.fontWeight, color: ts.color, background: s.backgroundColor,
      caretLeft: caret ? Math.round(caret.getBoundingClientRect().left) : null};
  });
  await trigger.click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(400);
  await page.mouse.move(0, 0);
  const menu = await triggerEl.evaluate((el) => {
    const m = (el.closest('aria-menu') ?? el.closest('.ui.dropdown') ?? el).querySelector('.menu');
    const ms = getComputedStyle(m);
    const items = [...m.querySelectorAll(':scope > .item')];
    const item = items[0];
    const is = getComputedStyle(item);
    const icon = item.querySelector('img, svg');
    return {
      box: m.getBoundingClientRect().toJSON(), radius: ms.borderRadius, shadow: ms.boxShadow, bg: ms.backgroundColor,
      itemHeights: items.map((i) => Math.round(i.getBoundingClientRect().height * 10) / 10),
      itemFont: `${is.fontSize} ${is.fontWeight} ${is.lineHeight}`, itemPadding: is.padding,
      iconOffset: icon ? {dx: Math.round(icon.getBoundingClientRect().left - item.getBoundingClientRect().left), dy: Math.round((icon.getBoundingClientRect().top - item.getBoundingClientRect().top) * 10) / 10, textGap: Math.round((() => { const r = document.createRange(); r.selectNodeContents(item); const rects = [...r.getClientRects()]; const last = rects.at(-1); return last.left - icon.getBoundingClientRect().right; })())} : null,
    };
  });
  menu.box = round(menu.box);
  out[name] = {trigger: triggerBefore, triggerStyle, menu};
}
console.log(JSON.stringify(out, null, 1));
await browser.close();
```

```bash
EOF
```

```typescript
import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import {login, apiCreateRepo, randomString, assertNoJsError} from './utils.ts';

const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;

test('add webhook menu adds a webhook by keyboard', async ({page, request}) => {
  const repoName = `e2e-add-webhook-${randomString(8)}`;
  await Promise.all([apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repoName}), login(page)]);
  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repoName}/settings/hooks`);
  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Add Webhook'});
  const menu = page.getByRole('menu', {name: 'Add Webhook'});

  await trigger.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Gitea'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Packagist'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(menu).toBeHidden();
  await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();

  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  await page.keyboard.press('d');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Discord'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('d');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'DingTalk'})).toBeFocused();
  // the button sits at the header's right edge, so the menu must open leftwards from it
  const triggerBox = (await trigger.boundingBox())!;
  const menuBox = (await menu.boundingBox())!;
  expect(menuBox.x + menuBox.width).toBeCloseTo(triggerBox.x + triggerBox.width, 0);

  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`/${repoName}/settings/hooks/dingtalk/new$`));
  const hookUrl = `https://example.com/${randomString(8)}`;
  await page.locator('#payload_url').fill(hookUrl);
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`/${repoName}/settings/hooks$`));
  await expect(page.getByText(hookUrl)).toBeVisible();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('webhook type switcher is named and switches type by keyboard', async ({page, request}) => {
  const repoName = `e2e-webhook-type-${randomString(8)}`;
  await Promise.all([apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repoName}), login(page)]);
  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repoName}/settings/hooks/dingtalk/new`);
  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Webhook type: DingTalk'});

  await expect(page.getByRole('menu', {name: 'Webhook type: DingTalk', includeHidden: true})).toHaveAttribute('id', (await trigger.getAttribute('aria-controls'))!);
  await trigger.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Gitea'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('s');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Slack'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`/${repoName}/settings/hooks/slack/new$`));
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Webhook type: Slack'})).toBeVisible();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

```

````text
======
# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.
````

```markdown
Closes #110

## What changed

Four Fomantic dropdown action menus on settings pages are now `<aria-menu>`:

- **Add Webhook**, in the shared `templates/repo/settings/webhook/base_list.tmpl`, so the repository, organisation, user and admin webhook pages all change at once (the admin page renders it twice).
- **The webhook type switcher** on the new and edit webhook forms (`templates/webhook/new.tmpl`). Its trigger is named "Webhook type: <type>" from the new key `repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher` (`"Webhook type: %s"`). The visible text and the label both come from one `$typeName` value, so they can't drift apart.
- **Link Account** on Settings → Security (`templates/user/settings/security/accountlinks.tmpl`).
- **Operations** above the System Notices table (`templates/admin/notice.tmpl`). The existing `.select.action` click handlers in `initAdminNotice` are unchanged, because `<aria-menu>` turns Enter and Space into `click()`.

So that the menus look the same as before (AC6), `web_src/css/modules/aria-menu.css` now copies what Fomantic gave them:

- Item text uses normal weight, so menus inside an `h4` header don't inherit its medium weight.
- `<img>` icons in items get Fomantic's spacing and vertical alignment. Most webhook icons and custom OAuth2 icons are `<img>`.
- A `.btn` trigger inherits its font weight (browsers reset it on buttons) and keeps the gap after a leading image.
- A neutral `.ui.button` trigger looks pressed while its menu is open, as `.ui.active.dropdown.button` did. This also brings back the pressed look on #108's Add File and folder menus.
- New `floating` host attribute for Fomantic's `ui floating dropdown` look: a 0.5em gap from the trigger and all corners rounded. It's documented in `aria.md` and in the `aria-menu.ts` header comment.

`web_src/css/modules/header.css` also drops the Fomantic margin from a button inside a header's `.ui.right` menu. Without that, the `bottom-end` menu would stick out 3px past the button.

## Why

Fomantic dropdowns keep focus on the wrapper and point at items with `aria-activedescendant`. With VoiceOver this breaks the arrow keys (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`). `<aria-menu>` moves real focus onto the items.

- **AC1:** Add Webhook is an `<aria-menu>` whose items are `link_menu.tmpl`'s links, with no `ui dropdown` class.
- **AC2:** the type switcher is an `<aria-menu>` named "Webhook type: Slack" (for example), not "Slack" alone.
- **AC3:** Link Account is an `<aria-menu>`, and each item links to `/user/oauth2/<name>`, path-escaped.
- **AC4:** Operations is an `<aria-menu placement="top-start">`. Select All, Deselect All and Inverse Selection work by keyboard and by mouse.
- **AC5:** Enter, Space and ArrowDown open each menu on its first item. Arrows, Home/End and type-ahead move focus. Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- **AC6:** position and look match in light and dark (screenshots below, with the small differences listed).
- **AC7:** the new Playwright tests cover adding a webhook and switching its type by keyboard, and the existing e2e and Go integration suites still pass.

## How it was tested

**Playwright: `tests/e2e/webhook-menus.test.ts` (new)**
- *Add webhook by keyboard*, from the repository settings page:
  - Enter opens on Gitea, End reaches Packagist, Escape returns focus.
  - Type-ahead `d` `d` moves Discord → DingTalk.
  - The menu's right edge lines up with the button (`bottom-end`).
  - Enter opens the DingTalk form. Pressing Enter in the URL field saves it, and the new webhook shows in the list.
- *Switch type by keyboard*:
  - The trigger and its menu are both named "Webhook type: DingTalk".
  - Enter, then `s`, focuses Slack, and Enter opens the Slack form.
  - The trigger is now named "Webhook type: Slack".

**Go integration**
- `TestNewWebHookLink` (updated): its old selector matches nothing after this change, and the test used to pass even when it found no items. It now checks that the list, new and edit pages contain `<aria-menu>` links and no Fomantic dropdown in the header (AC1/AC2).
- `TestUserSettingsSecurity/link_account_menu` (new): adds an OAuth2 source whose name contains spaces and checks for the escaped `/user/oauth2/test%20link%20source` item (AC3).

**Not covered by e2e, checked by hand instead**
- AC3 and AC4 behaviour would need an OAuth2 login source and system notices. The e2e helpers can't create either, since notices only come from failed mirror or user-deletion jobs.

  - The org, user and admin webhook lists: 11 items each, no Fomantic dropdown left.

## Screenshots (AC6)

Before | after, light | dark, at 1280×720 with each menu open.

<!-- drag in: 110-add-webhook.png, 110-type-switcher.png, 110-link-account.png, 110-notice-operations.png -->

Add Webhook, the type switcher and Link Account are identical. Operations has three small differences:

- **Items are 14px instead of 13px.** Fomantic sized the items from the button's `small` class, because the button and the dropdown were one element. The items now use the standard menu size, as the commit Operations menu has since #108.
- **The button is 3px narrower.** `.ui.dropdown.button` reserved 22px of right padding for a caret this button never had.
- **The gap above the button is 7px instead of 5.5px**, because it is 0.5em of the larger font.

Placement: Fomantic picked a direction each time a menu opened, flipping it when it ran out of room. `<aria-menu>` uses a fixed placement, so each menu is set to where it opened at normal widths: `bottom-end` for the three right-aligned menus and `top-start` for Operations. One difference: Link Account used to flip upward when the button was near the bottom of the window, and now it always opens downward.

## Design

This follows the issue's Decision 1 (change only the two templates that include `link_menu.tmpl`) and Decision 2 (an `aria-label` built from the same `$typeName` as the visible text). Two things were added during implementation: the `floating` host attribute, and the CSS rules above that keep the old look.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- `<aria-menu>` has no automatic flip, so each placement is fixed in its template. A menu near the bottom of the window now opens off-screen and the page has to scroll, where Fomantic flipped it upward (seen with Link Account).
- The look-alike rules copy Fomantic's numbers (`0.78571429rem`, `0.5em`).
- The pressed-trigger rule lists the coloured button variants (`:not(.primary, .red, .green)`), so a new coloured variant used as a trigger needs adding there.
- `floating` is a new host attribute that only Operations uses so far. The pulse and dashboard `ui floating dropdown jump` menus can use it when they move over.

**Encountered:**
- `TestNewWebHookLink` passed even when its selector matched nothing. It now asserts the item count.
- Several Fomantic quirks behind the old look: `.ui.small.dropdown` resizing its items, 22px caret padding on a button with no caret, `.ui.dropdown > .ui.button { margin: 0 }`, and the `active` class on the open dropdown. Each is either copied or explained above.
- `./.claude-students/check.sh` already fails on `main` because `models-issues.md` is over its line cap. Left for a separate chore.
```
